answer: Jury weight in this market comes only from fees paid by outside clients. When a client pays an agent, 10% of the fee burns as an ember, and the agent receives a marble: a signed receipt naming client, amount and burn. A key's timber, its voting weight, is the sum of marbles from clients whose funds never passed through a wallet that funded that key, and each marble expires after 60 days. A farm giving 1,000 fakes 100 timber each must route 100,000 units through unlinked wallets and lose 10,000 to embers, then pay that again every 60 days.
